newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GROSS FOREIGN DEBT $6.4BLN END-SEPT - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GROSS FOREIGN DEBT $6.4BLN END-SEPT - C.BANK.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Thursday the country's preliminary overall gross foreign debt totalled $6.34 billion in September, up from $5.8 billion at the end of 1995.

"The overall external debt stands at $6.34 billion, according to preliminary figures, of which less than $2.0 billion is official debt," Peter Balaz, head of the NBS Foreign Exchange Liabilities Department, told Reuters.
"From the capacities and abilities point of view, Slovakia has no problem redeeming its debt," he added.

"We have been redeeming the official debt for which the NBS acts as an agent without any problems since the very start in January 1993, and there is certainly no problem with the NBS yen-denominated bond issues either," Balaz said.
He added that he could not talk about the redemption of the remaining debt, which has been accrued by commercial banks and companies.
The NBS has placed two foreign bond issues totalling 50 billion yen to support Slovakia's balance of payments since 1993. Both were lead-managed by Nomura International Plc.
